Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

 New business and pipeline

ELYSIS – Directeur(trice), Ressources humaines et Communications 
 Une nouvelle ère pour l’industrie de l’aluminium – ELYSIS 
 Aluminium sans carbone 
 La technologie ELYSIS™ représente la plus grande avancée dans l’industrie de l’aluminium depuis 1886. Des efforts sont présentement déployés afin de perfectionner cette nouvelle façon révolutionnaire de produire de l’aluminium, qui élimine le dioxyde de carbone et toutes les autres émissions de gaz à effet de serre du procédé conventionnel d’électrolyse.
 Le procédé ELYSIS élimine l’utilisation d’anodes de carbone, en les remplaçant par des matériaux brevetés. En tant que premier procédé industriel qui émet de l’oxygène comme sous-produit, il a le potentiel de transformer toute l’industrie.
 En 2018, deux producteurs d’aluminium de calibre international, Alcoa et Rio Tinto, ont uni leurs forces afin de créer la coentreprise ELYSIS avec le gouvernement du Québec. Bénéficiant du soutien du gouvernement du Canada et d’Apple, la technologie progresse et elle est actuellement conçue pour être utilisée aussi bien dans des projets de construction que de modernisation d’alumineries. ELYSIS a son siège social à Montréal, avec des centres de recherche et de développement à Alma et à Jonquière, au Québec (Canada), ainsi qu’à New Kensington, en Pennsylvanie (États-Unis) et en France.
 En 2024, ELYSIS vend sa première licence commerciale à Rio Tinto dans le cadre du projet UDTE (Usine de Démonstration de la Technologie ELYSIS), situé à Arvida. Présentement, ELYSIS supporte son premier client pour les phases de préparation aux démarrages de cuves et à leur opération. 
 Joignez-vous à l’équipe d’ELYSIS !
 Relevant du PDG d’ELYSIS 
 Objectif du poste 
 Le ou la Directeur(trice), Ressources humaines et Communications est membre de l’équipe de direction d’ELYSIS et agit à titre de conseiller(ère) stratégique de confiance auprès du PDG pour toutes les questions liées aux personnes, à l’organisation, à la culture, au leadership et aux communications.
 Alors qu’ELYSIS poursuit l’avancement de sa technologie et de ses activités d’industrialisation, cette personne dirige la fonction RH et contribue au développement des capacités organisationnelles, du leadership et de la main-d’œuvre nécessaires à la réalisation des priorités stratégiques de l’entreprise.
 Évoluant au sein d’une coentreprise entre Rio Tinto et Alcoa, le rôle exige un solide sens des affaires, un jugement indépendant et la capacité d’équilibrer les besoins d’ELYSIS tout en maintenant des relations constructives avec les 
 actionnaires.
 À propos de vous 
 • Baccalauréat en ressources humaines, relations industrielles, administration des affaires ou dans un domaine connexe; une maîtrise ou une formation de deuxième cycle constitue un atout.
 • Minimum de 15 à 20 années d’expérience en ressources humaines, dont plusieurs années dans des postes de leadership RH senior.
 • Expérience significative dans des environnements industriels, un atout.
 Principales responsabilités 
 Partenariat stratégique et transformation organisationn elle 
 • Agir à titre de conseiller(ère) de confiance auprès du PDG et de l’équipe de direction sur les enjeux liés aux ressources humaines, à l’efficacité organisationnelle, à la culture et au leadership.
 • Apporter une perspective indépendante, remettre en question les hypothèses de façon constructive et soutenir les décisions organisationnelles complexes.
 • Diriger la planification stratégique de la main-d’œuvre, la conception organisationnelle et la planification de la relève.
 • Soutenir la transformation organisationnelle, l’industrialisation et le développement des capacités critiques.
 Leadership RH et efficacité opérationnell e 
 • Diriger la fonction Ressources humaines et assurer une prestation efficace et pragmatique des activités liées au recrutement, à la gestion de la performance, à la rémunération, à la gestion des talents et aux relations avec les employés.
 • Évaluer et faire évoluer le modèle opérationnel RH, les capacités de l’équipe et l’utilisation des ressources internes et externes afin de répondre aux besoins changeants de l’entreprise.
 • Maintenir une collaboration efficace avec les politiques, processus et services RH de Rio Tinto et d’Alcoa.
 • Établir des priorités RH claires, ainsi que des responsabilités et des modes de collaboration efficaces.
 Culture, leadership et communication s 
 • Renforcer l’efficacité du leadership, la responsabilisation et la collaboration entre les différentes fonctions et les différents sites.
 • Accompagner les leaders de haut niveau et soutenir les initiatives de changement organisationnel et d’engagement des employés.
 • Diriger les communications internes en cohérence avec les priorités d’affaires et les transformations organisationnelles.
 • Conseiller le PDG et l’équipe de direction sur les communications organisationnelles sensibles et coordonner, au besoin, les communications corporatives avec les partenaires concernés.
 Relations avec les employés et gestion des dossiers sensibles 
 • Fournir des conseils stratégiques dans les dossiers complexes de relations de travail, les mesures disciplinaires, les cessations d’emploi et les réorganisations sensibles.
 • Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes juridiques, les équipes RH des actionnaires et les conseillers externes, au besoin.
 • Assurer un équilibre entre la gestion des risques, l’équité, le bon jugement et les exigences opérationnelles.
 Gouvernance de la coentreprise et relations avec les actionnaires 
 • Établir et maintenir des relations solides avec les leaders RH et les principales parties prenantes de Rio Tinto et d’Alcoa.
 • Naviguer dans les attentes des actionnaires, les exigences de gouvernance et les complexités organisationnelles.
 • Soutenir le PDG sur les questions liées aux ressources humaines et à l’organisation impliquant le conseil d’administration et les actionnaires.
 • Formuler des recommandations indépendantes alignées sur les intérêts et les priorités d’ELYSIS.
 Modèle opérationnel RH et principales relation s 
 Le ou la Directeur(trice) est responsable de l’efficacité globale de la fonction Ressources humaines. La structure de l’équipe, la répartition des responsabilités ainsi que l’équilibre entre les ressources internes et externes seront évaluées avec le PDG et pourront évoluer en fonction des besoins de l’entreprise.
 Les principales relations comprennent le PDG, l’équipe de direction d’ELYSIS, le conseil d’administration, les leaders fonctionnels et de sites, l’équipe RH, le service juridique, les partenaires en communications ainsi que les équipes RH et centres d’expertise de Rio Tinto et d’Alcoa.
 Expérience et compétences recherchées 
 • Expérience significative à un poste de leadership senior en ressources humaines, incluant un partenariat direct avec un PDG ou une équipe de direction.
 • Expérience démontrée en transformation organisationnelle, en planification de la main-d’œuvre et en développement du leadership.
 • Expérience dans un environnement industriel, technologique ou axé sur les projets; une expérience en coentreprise ou en structure matricielle constitue un atout.
 • Solide expertise en relations de travail et excellent jugement dans la gestion de situations délicates liées aux employés.
 • Approche orientée vers les affaires, pragmatique et à l’aise dans un environnement en évolution où l’ambiguïté est présente.
 • Crédibilité auprès des dirigeants, indépendance de jugement et capacité à remettre en question les décisions de manière constructive.
 • Excellentes habiletés en gestion des parties prenantes et capacité à établir des relations de confiance à travers différentes organisations.
 • Expérience démontrée dans le développement, l’encadrement et la mobilisation d’une équipe RH.
 • Maîtrise du français et de l'anglais, tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit. Notre organisation est une entreprise mondiale et les fonctions de ce poste nécessitent une collaboration quotidienne avec des collègues, des équipes ou des partenaires basés à l'extérieur du Québec
 Attentes en matière de leadership 
 La personne retenue alliera réflexion stratégique et exécution concrète, démontrera un fort engagement envers les priorités d’ELYSIS et agira comme partenaire de confiance du PDG.
 Le poste exige la capacité de représenter les intérêts d’ELYSIS de façon indépendante tout en maintenant des relations constructives et collaboratives avec Rio Tinto et Alcoa.
 À propos de nous 
 Un partenariat de classe mondiale sans précédent entre deux grands pionniers de l’industrie de l’aluminium – Alcoa et Rio Tinto – a donné lieu à la création d’ELYSIS en 2018. Dans le cadre de cette coentreprise avec le gouvernement du Québec, l’équipe travaille à développer la technologie en vue de sa commercialisation à grande échelle. 
 La technologie ELYSIS™ élimine toutes les émissions directes de gaz à effet de serre (GES) du procédé d’électrolyse de l’aluminium. Il s’agit du premier procédé industriel émettant de l’oxygène comme sous-produit. ELYSIS a démontré sa capacité à produire de l’aluminium de qualité commerciale auprès d’utilisateurs finaux allant d’Apple à Audi, et la technologie est actuellement conçue pour être utilisée aussi bien dans des projets de construction que de modernisation d’alumineries. 
 Lieu de travail 
 Canada
 Poste basé à Montréal, avec environ 25 % de déplacements (Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean, États-Unis et France).
 Faites partie d’un partenariat sans précédent
 Dans l’équipe d’ELYSIS, nous sommes déterminés à créer un milieu inclusif où les employés se sentent à l’aise d’être eux-mêmes. Nous souhaitons que notre équipe ait l’impression que sa voix compte, que toutes les cultures sont respectées et que les points de vue, aussi variés soient-ils, sont non seulement bienvenus, mais également essentiels au succès du partenariat sans précédent qu’est ELYSIS. Nous faisons preuve de respect mutuel, d’équité, de compassion et de dignité, sans égard aux questions d’origine ethnoculturelle, de sexe, de nationalité, de religion, d’âge, d’orientation sexuelle ou de tout autre aspect. 
 ELYSIS accueille favorablement et encourage les candidatures de personnes autochtones, de femmes, de membres de la communauté LGBTQ2S+, de personnes plus âgées, de personnes handicapées et de personnes d’origines diverses.

 Location: Canada 
 Montréal, with approximately 25% travel (Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean, United States and France).
 About Us 
 An unprecedented world-class partnership of two major aluminium industry pioneers – Alcoa and Rio Tinto – led to the 2018 formation of ELYSIS. Through this joint venture with the government of Québec, ELYSIS is working to scale up this technology so it can be fully commercialized.
 The ELYSIS™ technology eliminates all direct greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the aluminium smelting process and is the first industrial process that emits oxygen as its by-product.
 ELYSIS has demonstrated production of commercial purity aluminium for end users ranging from Apple to Audi and is being designed for the construction of new smelters or to retrofit existing ones.
 The ELYSIS™ technology also brings additional advantages, reducing the operating cost of a smelter and boosting metal production from the same size-smelting cell.

About Faire 
 Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.
 We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.
 About this role 
 Faire's Ads team helps brands succeed by putting them in charge of their own growth. We own the brand-facing side of the Ads business: the ads manager, campaign setup, performance reporting, budget retention and expansion, and the trust that keeps advertisers investing with us.
 As a product engineer on the team, you'll own features end-to-end: dig into the advertiser's problem, weigh the options, ship, and measure whether it worked. You'll partner with Product, Design, Data Science, and our Go-to-Market team to shape what we build, not just how it gets built.
 This is an ideal role for engineers who combine strong product intuition with genuine excitement about AI. You'll go deep on how ads work in a wholesale marketplace, where the advertisers are independent brands and the buyers are the retailers who stock them.
 What you'll do 
 Product ownership: Take advertiser-facing features from problem to launch, including ads manager workflows, campaign controls, and performance reporting.
 Product judgment: Partner closely with Product, Design, Data Science, Analytics, and Marketing to identify business opportunities and execute on them. Bring customer empathy for brand advertisers, a clear point of view, and a bias for delivering over waiting for a perfect spec.
 Technical craft: Build scalable systems and product experiences that stay fast and reliable as our advertiser base grows, and contribute to the technical strategy that gets us there.
 AI fluency: Use AI tooling as a core part of how you deliver impact, from prototyping and coding to reviewing and exploring ideas faster.
 Data fluency: Instrument what you ship, then use the data to understand advertiser behavior, evaluate experiment results, and guide where we invest next.
 Qualifications 
 Must-haves 
 2+ years of full-time software engineering experience shipping product in a production environment.
 Strong product judgment and customer empathy. You think about what to build, not just how, and you've shipped features you can explain in terms of who used them and what changed.
 Has integrated AI tools into your regular engineering workflow; we want to see that AI has become part of how you work, not just something you've tried.
 Background in at least one of: ads / ad tech, large analytics or measurement products, or data engineering (pipelines, ETL, warehousing).
 Able to thrive in a high-pace product environment; a clear communicator who works effectively with PMs, designers, data scientists and our Go-to-Market team.
 Preferred 
 Experience with ads manager, campaign management, or other advertiser-facing tools.
 More than one of the domain backgrounds above (ads + analytics, analytics + data engineering, etc.).
 Hands-on frontend experience with React or similar.
 Experience with experimentation or customer-facing reporting.
 Salary range 
 Canada: the pay range for this role is $129,500 - $ 178,000 per year. 
 This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors such as transferable skills, work experience, market demands, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.
 Hybrid Faire employees currently go into the office 3 days per week on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and a third flex day of their choosing (Monday, Wednesday, or Friday). Additionally, hybrid in-office roles will have the flexibility to work remotely up to 4 weeks per year. Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting. 
 Why you’ll love working at Faire 
 Flexible paid time off, plus company-wide recharge days
 Paid parental leave up to 16 weeks
 Comprehensive health coverage, with options varying by location
 Fertility and family-building benefits through Carrot, including a lifetime reimbursement allowance
 Mental health support and coaching through Modern Health
 Stipends to support your professional development, wellness, and work from home needs
 Employer-sponsored retirement plan, dependent on country of employment
 Faire was founded in 2017 by a team of early product and engineering leads from Square. We’re backed by some of the top investors in retail and tech including: Y Combinator, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Forerunner Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, and DST Global. We have headquarters in San Francisco and Kitchener-Waterloo, and a global employee presence across offices in Toronto, London, and New York. To learn more about Faire and our customers, you can read more on our blog .
 Faire provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression.
 Faire is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process and applicants with a disability may request to be accommodated throughout the recruitment process. We will work with all applicants to accommodate their individual accessibility needs. To request reasonable accommodation, please fill out our Accommodation Request Form ( https://bit.ly/faire-form) 
 Privacy 
 For information about the type of personal data Faire collects from applicants, as well as your choices regarding the data collected about you, please visit Faire’s Privacy Notice (https://www.faire.com/privacy)

Acumatica's Product Marketing team is looking for a strategic Product Marketer to own the product marketing for our QuickBooks Graduates program — the positioning, messaging, and content strategy that helps growing small businesses "graduate" from QuickBooks to a modern, cloud ERP platform. You have proven experience in ERP or SMB accounting/finance software, and a strong point of view on why and when small businesses outgrow QuickBooks. You'll craft compelling, differentiated messaging that speaks to QuickBooks users at the exact moment they're hitting the ceiling of their current system, and you'll tailor that story to the industries where those breaking points show up most: construction, manufacturing, distribution, professional services, and their related micro-verticals. This role is a full-time opportunity reporting directly to the VP of Product Marketing. 
 Primary Responsibilities: 
 QuickBooks Graduates Positioning & Storytelling 
 Own the positioning and messaging that fuels the QuickBooks Graduates program, working alongside marketing teams, sales, and partner teams who drive its broader execution. Shape clear, compelling narratives that translate product functionality into meaningful business value for small businesses that have outgrown QuickBooks — helping prospects understand not just what Acumatica does differently, but why it matters at their stage of growth, while clearly differentiating our cloud ERP platform from QuickBooks and other SMB accounting and.ERP tools. 
 Industry & Micro-Vertical Messaging 
 Go beyond a one-size-fits-all QuickBooks-replacement narrative. Build and maintain positioning and content that applies the QuickBooks Graduates story to our targeted industries — construction, manufacturing, distribution, and professional services — and their related micro-verticals, so messaging speaks directly to the specific triggers, workflows, and pain points that push each industry beyond QuickBooks. 
 Thought Leadership & Market Insight 
 Create differentiated thought leadership assets, messaging, and positioning that establish Acumatica as the trusted destination for growing QuickBooks customers. Ground our storytelling in an ideal customer profile — the QuickBooks user hitting the limits of their system — along with industry and market insights, to ensure our communications deeply resonate with real-world growing pains: multi-entity complexity, inventory and job costing limitations, lack of automation, and reporting gaps. 
 Go-to-Market Leadership 
 Work collaboratively with the broader marketing organization to support end-to-end go-to-market strategies for QuickBooks Graduates campaigns. 
 Customer-Centered Narratives 
 Partner with our customer advocacy team to review and elevate customer stories and videos from businesses that made the switch from QuickBooks, weaving authentic, real-world outcomes — by industry — into marketing assets. Use customer evidence to build trust, credibility, and emotional connection across the buyer journey. 
 Cross-Functional Collaboration 
 Work hand-in-hand with product, sales, and industry/vertical teams to stay aligned on roadmaps, priorities, and upcoming capabilities relevant to QuickBooks migration. Serve as a connective tissue across teams, ensuring marketing materials accurately reflect product evolution while amplifying shared goals. 
 Data-Informed Strategy 
 Leverage performance data and analytics to guide QuickBooks Graduates marketing strategies, evolve content, and evaluate campaign effectiveness by industry segment, and continuously refine our approach — balancing insight with creativity to drive stronger outcomes. 
 Content Experiences & Demos 
 Create engaging video scripts and perform light video edits in collaboration with professional design and video partners. Develop polished QuickBooks-comparison and product overview videos, along with intuitive, point-and-click demos that bring key workflows and "how-to" scenarios to life for growing businesses in our targeted industries. 
 Marketing Enablement 
 Maintain and evolve core QuickBooks Graduates assets — including website messaging, comparison guides, datasheets, infographics, brochures etc. — for both the overarching program and its industry-specific variants, to ensure clarity, consistency, and accuracy. Support release planning and help keep internal and external teams aligned on positioning as offerings grow and change. 
 Events, Speaking & Community Engagement 
 Support industry trade shows and events with strong messaging and content targeted at QuickBooks users evaluating a move to ERP. Contribute to partner and customer events through presentations, webinars, and thought leadership sessions — including opportunities to present live — sharing Acumatica's vision and expertise with confidence and authenticity. 
 Messaging and Positioning 
 Translate functionality and benefits into real value that resonate with small business buyers, tailoring that value story to both the overarching QuickBooks Graduates program and its industry-specific extensions.
Experience: A minimum of three to five years of product marketing experience is required. You must possess a deep knowledge of small business accounting software (QuickBooks or comparable), ERP business management systems, accounting processes, business technology, and B2B marketing strategies. Experience marketing to or supporting one or more of the following industries is a plus: construction, manufacturing, distribution, or professional services. 
 Education: An educational background in marketing, English, public relations, journalism, business, philosophy, computer science, or a related field.

You must approach every project with an analytical mind and a creative approach to messaging. Excellent organization, multitasking ability, and strong communication are essential.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



As a Staff Demo Engineer on the Demo Engineering team, you’ll shape the technical tooling and platform behind 1Password’s go-to-market demo experience. You’ll build scalable demo environments, interactive product experiences, and shared infrastructure that help teams communicate 1Password’s value across the customer journey. Your work will help make secure access simpler and support 1Password’s mission to create a safer, simpler digital future for everyone.



How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.



What we're looking for:

 - Bring substantial experience in software engineering, cloud engineering, platform engineering, technical marketing, DevOps, solutions architecture, or demo engineering.

 - Apply experience in cybersecurity, identity, Privileged Access Management (PAM), developer tools, or a related technical domain.

 - Build full-stack and automation solutions using technologies such as TypeScript, JavaScript, Node.js, React, or Python, with experience designing systems that other engineers can build on.

 - Design and operate infrastructure using infrastructure as code, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), containers, and cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

 - Understand identity and access management concepts, including single sign-on (SSO), Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML), OpenID Connect (OIDC), System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), device trust, passwordless authentication, and passkeys.

 - Balance speed, reliability, cost, and security while explaining technical tradeoffs clearly to technical and non-technical partners.

 - Create interactive software-as-a-service (SaaS) demos and guided product experiences using platforms such as Reprise, Navattic, Walnut, or Arcade; experience with mobile device management (MDM) tools such as Jamf, live event demos, utilization analysis, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted tooling, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers is also valuable.



What you can expect:

 - Set the technical vision, roadmap, and long-term architecture for 1Password’s demo platform.

 - Lead the design of shared demo infrastructure, including templates, automated provisioning and resets, data generation, and observability.

 - Build sample applications and integrations across 1Password products to support demos and enablement programs.

 - Support complex, high-visibility demos for flagship launches, keynotes, conferences, and strategic customer opportunities.

 - Drive AI-assisted tooling that automates demo preparation, validation, and maintenance.

 - Partner with Engineering Security on demo environments and lead architecture and code reviews.

 - Mentor Demo Engineers and Senior Demo Engineers while representing Demo Engineering in cross-functional technical decisions and product roadmap discussions.

 Educational Assistants are an integral part of a dynamic and collaborative team, who work supporting students requiring behavioural supports and/or complex physical disabilities/developmental delays and will be expected to assume other duties, as required. 
 What will you do? 
 Applicants will work as a team to support students from Kindergarten to Grade 12 with varying needs, including behavioural challenges and/or complex physical disabilities, developmental delays and/or severe medical needs. Duties will include ensuring all students’ safety at all times, implementing individualized programs and carrying out Positive Behaviour Support Plans as developed by the student’s Learning Team. Lethbridge School Division makes every effort to ensure staff and student safety, while understanding not every behaviour on the part of students, can be anticipated. Targeted behaviours may include, but are not limited to, severe opposition, hitting, kicking, spitting, biting, scratching, and throwing of objects and the use of inappropriate and/or threatening language. Specialized training such as Supporting Individuals through Valued Attachments (SIVA) would be an asset.
 Hours will vary between 0 - 29.5 hours Monday to Friday dependent on Division needs.
 What do you need to succeed? 
 Training and/or experience working with students with severe behaviour challenges is necessary as well as an understanding of neurodiversity, such as ASD, ODD, FASD, ADHD and/or other behavioural disabilities. Preference will be given to the candidate with proven experience executing Positive Behavior Support Plans. Training and/or experience supporting students with Occupational Therapy/Physical Therapy and/or Speech-Language acquisition needs would be an asset.
 Lethbridge School Division embraces a philosophy/belief of inclusion for all students. Consequently, the successful candidate must have a willingness to provide personal care, lifting, and toileting support for students, with appropriate assistance and/or training provided as needed. The successful candidate may also be required to participate in community activities such as swimming and skating. Educational Assistants may also be working with students with limited experience within formal school settings and may support students with English as an additional language. 
 A strong understanding of Trauma Informed practice, resiliency, building connections, self-regulation supports and strategies, and conflict resolution skills is an asset.  Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on electric and autonomous vehicles used in robotaxi fleet operations .
 Ensure vehicles are technically ready for daily deployment, testing, commercial operations, and autonomous ride-hailing services .

 Diagnose and repair mechanical, electrical, electronic, and software-related vehicle issues.

We do the research, content, distribution and optimization that build a brand's presence where AI and buyers look: LLMs, search, Reddit and YouTube.  Own video quality standards and the QA process across every video we ship, from script to final cut.
 Source, vet and manage video vendors and freelancers (editors, scriptwriters, creators). Hold them to quality, turnaround and cost.
 Build a repeatable production workflow, including in-house editing and scriptwriting where it beats outsourcing on quality or cost.
 Track cost per video and keep the program inside budget.
 Coach our creative producer and video strategists on production, feedback and client handling.

 10+ years in video or film production, including creative director or senior producer roles.
 Experience running video at volume across multiple vendors and freelancers.
 A working knowledge of YouTube: titles, hooks, retention, search and how videos get discovered.
 Confidence with clients. You can defend a creative call to a senior marketer and keep the relationship strong.

 Comfort working fractionally: async-first, decisive, and focused on the highest-leverage problems.

 A video QA checklist and review process used on every video before it ships.
 A vendor audit covering quality, cost per video and turnaround, with a recommendation for each vendor.
 A documented production workflow from brief to publish, including the in-house editing and scripting pilots.
 A cost-per-video baseline and target, agreed with leadership.

 Fewer revision rounds and faster turnaround from brief to publish.

 Position Summary 
 The Senior Quality Assurance Analyst works closely with product, development, design, infrastructure, and other QA team members to deliver reliable and accessible digital learning products. This role is responsible for testing web applications across the frontend and backend using manual, API, database, automation, accessibility, and performance testing methods.
 The successful candidate will take part in quality activities throughout the software development lifecycle. This includes planning, design reviews, test preparation, testing, defect investigation, release validation, and production regression testing.
 This position will primarily support product development. The QA Manager may also assign a portion of the analyst’s time to infrastructure, platform, performance, or other technical initiatives based on team priorities.
 The regular work schedule is 1:00 PM to 9:00 PM Eastern Time to provide coverage for teams working in the Pacific Time Zone.
Responsibilities 
 Create, maintain, and execute test plans, test scenarios, and test cases for web applications.
 Test frontend and backend functionality, including user interfaces, APIs, databases, integrations, and services.
 Perform functional, regression, smoke, exploratory, integration, usability, and cross browser testing.
 Find, reproduce, investigate, and document defects in Jira with clear steps, evidence, expected results, and actual results.
 Work closely with developers, product managers, designers, infrastructure engineers, and other stakeholders to investigate and resolve quality issues.
 Validate that completed work meets functional requirements, acceptance criteria, design expectations, and quality standards.
 Create, maintain, execute, and improve automated tests using Playwright or similar modern automation tools.
 Help improve the structure, reliability, coverage, and maintainability of the automated regression suite.
 Use AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Codex, or similar tools to support test development, troubleshooting, documentation, and other QA activities when appropriate.
 Create and maintain clear QA documentation, testing standards, and reusable testing practices.
 Participate in release testing and help identify quality risks before changes are released.
 Stay familiar with the functionality of Nelson products and understand how educators and learners use them in the classroom.
 Infrastructure, Observability and Performance Testing
 The Senior QA Analyst may occasionally support infrastructure and platform testing. The goal is to help the team investigate issues using technical evidence and identify regressions before they reach customers.
 Use telemetry signals such as logs, traces, and metrics to support defect investigation, bug triage, and root cause analysis.
 Review distributed traces to identify suspicious backend calls, service interactions, API requests, or gRPC calls related to a reported issue.
 Use telemetry data to help confirm whether a reported problem is reproducible and to provide useful technical evidence to development and infrastructure teams.
 Create and execute load and performance tests using k6 or similar tools.
 Use load tests as part of regression testing to identify changes in application or service performance.
 Review performance measurements such as response time, throughput, error rate, and percentile latency including p95 latency.
 Compare performance results against previous results or established baselines to identify possible regressions.
 Work with developers and infrastructure engineers to investigate performance issues such as increased latency, excessive service calls, request fanout, or unexpected backend activity.
 Assist with release and production readiness testing when performance or infrastructure validation is required.
 Experience and Qualifications 
 4 or more years of professional experience in software quality assurance or software testing, preferably with web based applications.
 Strong experience testing modern web applications across both frontend and backend systems.
 Hands-on experience testing APIs, databases, integrations, and other backend services.
 Experience creating test plans, test strategies, test scenarios, and detailed test cases.
 Experience designing, writing, and maintaining automated tests. Experience with Playwright is strongly preferred.
 Good understanding of web application architecture, frontend and backend systems, APIs, databases, services, and common security concepts.
 Experience using Jira or a similar issue tracking system to manage defects and testing work.
 Experience working in Agile and Scrum development environments with designers, developers, product managers, and other QA professionals.
 Experience with accessibility testing and knowledge of AODA or related accessibility standards.
 Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills. Able to investigate an issue beyond the visible user interface and provide useful evidence to the team.
 Clear written and verbal communication skills. Able to explain defects and technical findings in simple and concise language.
 Ability to manage multiple priorities and move between product, automation, release, and infrastructure testing when needed.
 Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively with cross functional teams.
 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Working knowledge of application observability and telemetry, including logs, distributed traces, and metrics.
 Experience using observability tools such as Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry, Application Insights, or similar platforms.
 Experience with performance and load testing using k6 or a similar tool.
 Ability to understand performance measurements such as p95 latency, throughput, response time, and error rate.
 Experience using telemetry and traces to support root cause analysis and defect investigation.
 Experience testing service based or microservice architectures, including REST APIs or gRPC services.
 Experience using AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Codex, or similar tools as part of software development or QA workflows.
 Experience contributing to automation frameworks, continuous integration workflows, or automated regression pipelines.
 Experience testing education technology, content platforms, learning applications, or other customer facing digital products is an asset.

About RIC Power Corporation: 
 RIC Power Corporation, a Panelmatic Company, is a leading custom manufacturer of medium voltage switchgear, protection, and control systems. We pride ourselves on engineering excellence and delivering high-quality, reliable solutions to our clients across various industries. Join a team dedicated to innovation and quality in a stable and supportive environment.
 Position Summary: 
 We are seeking an experienced Senior Test Technician to join our QC & Testing team. This position is primarily facility-based (approx. 95% in-shop, ~5% on-site/remote field support) and is responsible for independently performing full electrical functional and high-voltage apparatus testing on newly manufactured low and medium voltage switchgear and control systems, in addition to mentoring Test Technicians and supporting the Engineering Quality Lead on Factory Acceptance Testing and test plan development.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Electrical Functionality Testing: Independently perform full functional testing of protection and control schemes, including control power distribution, protection relay operation, breaker close/open logic, and interlocks.
 HV Apparatus Testing: Independently conduct high-voltage apparatus testing, including Hi-Pot, Partial Discharge (PD), BIL, Heat Run, and Contact Resistance testing.
 Interlock Defeat & Mechanical Safety Verification: Independently perform interlock defeat and mechanical safety verification (door/racking interlocks, TOC/MOC status, etc.) under controlled conditions.
 Visual, Mechanical & Point-to-Point Backup: Perform or back up Visual & BOM confirmation, mechanical functionality confirmation, and Point-to-Point continuity testing as needed.
 Minor Defect Correction: Directly fix connection-integrity issues you personally find during your own testing (e.g., a loose or under-torqued connection that already matches the drawing package), without escalation. Anything that does not match the drawing package is flagged back to Production for rework.
 Electrical Code & Standards: Know and apply relevant electrical codes and standards (CSA, IEEE, UL, etc.) during testing.
 Test Plans & Reports: Contribute technical input into test plan development and final test reports (does not author).
 Troubleshooting: Independently troubleshoot and resolve design- or production-related issues in collaboration with Engineering.
 FAT & Field Support: Lead or back up Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT), and independently provide on-site or remote field support (~5%) when required.
 Mentorship & Production Feedback: Provide informal, on-the-floor guidance to Test Technicians during testing, and, alongside the Engineering Quality Lead, feed findings back to the Production team for learning and improvement.
 Safety Practice: Work independently and safely, including on energized work; identify and contribute hazards to Job Hazard Analyses (JHA). Stop-work authority applies regardless of tier: halt any test you believe is unsafe.
 ISO/QMS Contribution: Contribute to ISO/QMS process improvement.
 Equipment & Supplier Inspection: Verify your own test equipment is current before use, and back up Supplier & incoming-inspection quality checks as needed.
 Required Qualifications: 
 Education & Experience: Diploma or Degree in Electrical Engineering, with 3+ years of experience in low and medium voltage switchgear and power apparatus testing.
 Technical Expertise: Expert at interpreting complex electrical drawings and performing hands-on testing.
 Safety: Demonstrated ability to work independently and safely on energized/high-voltage tasks.
 Soft Skills: Strong troubleshooting abilities, high attention to detail, and proficiency in MS Office for technical reporting.
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 FAT Experience: Experience with Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) procedures.
 Standards Knowledge: Working knowledge of relevant industry standards (e.g., CSA, IEEE, ANSI, NETA, UL).
 Network Testing: Familiarity with communication network testing.

Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



Our Infrastructure Services organization is responsible for the underlying infrastructure that powers the 1Password application. It includes Compute Services, Network and Edge Services, and Stateful Services.



As a Senior Staff Cloud Platform Engineer, you set the multi-year technical strategy for Infrastructure Services. You decide where the organization invests, define the architecture and standards that every infrastructure team and internal tenant builds on, and make sure our compute, network and edge, and stateful platforms evolve as one coherent system rather than three separate ones. You partner with engineering and product leadership, security, and finance to balance reliability, security, cost, and delivery speed, and you are the senior technical voice for infrastructure across the company.



This is a hands-on role. You write design docs, prototype, review the hardest designs, and step into the most serious incidents. But your main impact comes from making many teams more effective and from the decisions that hold up for years.



How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.



What we're looking for:

 - You have set technical direction across multiple teams. You have owned an infrastructure strategy or architecture spanning several teams or an entire organization, and you can point to the multi-year outcomes: what others adopted, what shipped, and what measurably improved.

 - You have operated Kubernetes at production scale. This includes multi-cluster, multi-tenant, customer-traffic-bearing environments (EKS or similar managed platforms preferred). You know it deeply, from autoscaling and admission control to GitOps, workload identity, and fleet-wide cluster upgrades.

 - You combine depth with breadth. Beyond Kubernetes, you have working fluency in networking and edge and in stateful data systems, and you understand how a decision in one layer affects the rest.

 - You have made reliability a standard, not a project. You defined SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets, and you got multiple teams to adopt them. You have improved incident response, post-incident learning, and disaster recovery across an organization, not just on your own team.

 - You have cut cloud costs through engineering. You can show measurable, real-dollar impact from work such as capacity automation, right-sizing, architecture changes, or commitment strategy, and you have worked with finance on forecasting and tradeoffs.

 - You build security in by design. You have driven practices such as workload identity, least-privilege IAM and RBAC, credential rotation, and strong isolation in multi-tenant environments, and you have partnered with security teams on risk decisions and compliance requirements.

 - You still build. You are proficient in Go (or a similar language) and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), and you have a track record of automating complex, high-toil operational workflows at fleet scale.

 - You influence without relying on authority. You write clear strategy and design documents, present to senior leaders, resolve technical disagreements between teams, and build alignment on difficult tradeoffs.

 - You grow other engineers. You have mentored Senior and Staff engineers, raised the bar on design review, and helped shape how your organization hires and evaluates technical talent.



Bonus points for:

 - Hands-on experience with service mesh and service-to-service networking, such as Linkerd or Amazon VPC Lattice.

 - Experience operating scalable database technology, such as MySQL, Postgres, or DynamoDB.

 - Designing developer platform abstractions for internal teams, such as paved-road service toolkits and production readiness frameworks, that measurably improved usability and productivity.

 - Helping build AI-assisted operations tools, such as auto-remediation or AI-assisted diagnosis, rather than only using them.

 - Operating highly available, multi-region services in a large SaaS environment, including capacity planning and performance optimization at scale.

 - Experience in a security, identity, or other high-trust product environment.



What you can expect:

 - Set the multi-year technical strategy and architecture for Infrastructure Services, working with directors and senior engineering leadership to shape roadmap and investment decisions, including build versus buy.

 - Define the patterns, standards, and guardrails across compute, network and edge, and stateful services that internal teams depend on for years.

 - Represent Infrastructure Services in cross-organization reviews with product engineering, security, and finance, and serve as the senior technical voice for the platform.

 - Serve as an escalation point for major incidents, and drive organization-wide improvements to incident management, reliability targets, and disaster recovery.

 - Lead cost, capacity, and efficiency strategy for our cloud footprint, with measurable goals.

 - Drive adoption of automation and AI-assisted operations to reduce toil across the organization.

 - Mentor Staff and Senior engineers, raise the bar on design review and engineering practice, and help us hire and develop the next generation of infrastructure leaders.

 Ce que vous ferez
 Allons-y. Changeons le monde. 
 Le ou la gestionnaire, relations stratégiques avec les pharmacies, Québec, est responsable d’établir et de gérer des relations stratégiques avec les parties prenantes du secteur pharmaceutique au Québec ainsi qu’avec les canaux émergents d’engagement des patients soutenus par les pharmacies, afin de faire progresser l’accès des patients, l’engagement des pharmaciens et les priorités d’affaires de l’Unité d’affaires Médecine générale (GMBU), avec un accent principal sur les domaines cardiovasculaire et cardiométabolique.
 Responsabilités clés
 1. Stratégie pharmaceutique au Québec et planification des comptes
 Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’engagement propres au Québec, alignées sur les priorités de la GMBU dans les canaux de pharmacies communautaires, spécialisées et numériques.
 Responsabilités : 
 Élaborer et maintenir des plans de comptes stratégiques pour les organisations pharmaceutiques prioritaires, les bannières/chaînes, les associations, les partenaires en pharmacie spécialisée et les canaux numériques d’engagement des patients.
 Bâtir et entretenir un réseau de parties prenantes et de décideurs clés du secteur pharmaceutique partout au Québec.
 Repérer des occasions d’améliorer l’éducation des patients, l’accès, l’amorce du traitement, l’observance, la persistance au traitement et le soutien aux patients.
 Produire des perspectives de marché sur la pratique en pharmacie, les parcours des patients, le remboursement, l’activité concurrentielle et les modèles de soins émergents.
 Transformer les perspectives pharmaceutiques et de marché en recommandations concrètes pour les partenaires interfonctionnels.
 2. Gestion des relations avec les parties prenantes
 Agir comme personne-ressource principale pour les comptes pharmaceutiques clés, les organisations et les partenaires numériques du secteur pharmaceutique.
 Collaborer avec les propriétaires de pharmacies, les pharmaciens, les leaders de bannières, les partenaires en pharmacie spécialisée, les associations et les intervenants en soins virtuels de manière conforme et axée sur la valeur.
 Représenter Amgen lors de rencontres avec les clients, de conférences et de forums sectoriels pertinents.
 Faciliter la collaboration entre les parties prenantes externes et les équipes internes interfonctionnelles.
 3. Création de valeur et initiatives axées sur le patient
 Cerner et co-créer des initiatives fondées sur la pharmacie qui soutiennent l’éducation des patients, l’accès, l’observance et le soutien aux patients dans les domaines cardiovasculaire et cardiométabolique.
 Collaborer avec les équipes internes afin de développer des ressources, outils et modèles de service conformes.

 Évaluer les résultats des initiatives et tirer parti des apprentissages pour améliorer les programmes à venir.

 Informer les parties prenantes internes des tendances du marché, des besoins des clients et des occasions stratégiques.
 Collaborer avec la personne responsable de la pharmacie à l’échelle nationale afin d’harmoniser les priorités du Québec avec la stratégie pharmaceutique nationale.

 Collaborer avec les équipes de l’accès au marché, des affaires médicales, des services aux patients, des ventes, du marketing, des affaires juridiques, de la conformité, des affaires réglementaires, des affaires gouvernementales et d’autres fonctions clés.

ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.



THE ROLE

We're looking for distributed systems engineers and product-minded generalists to build the distributed runtime that powers large-scale LLM inference on Baseten. Our inference platform empowers customers to deploy and operate cutting-edge models with industry-leading performance, scalability, and reliability. It also powers Model APIs, our hosted endpoints for the latest open-source models. You'll work across the stack, from the developer experience customers use to deploy models, through the libraries behind features like tool calling and reasoning, down to the systems that orchestrate deployments on Kubernetes and route traffic efficiently. Your job is to make sure every model on our platform is fast, reliable, and cost-efficient. You'll join a small, high-impact team at the intersection of distributed systems, model performance, infrastructure, and product, helping define how developers use AI models at scale. This role is ideal for engineers who enjoy owning systems in production, solving hard integration problems, and making complex infrastructure simple and reliable for users.

 

EXAMPLE INITIATIVES

You'll get to work on these types of projects on our Inference Platform:

 - The Baseten Inference Stack at NVIDIA Dynamo Day https://www.baseten.co/blog/nvidia-dynamo-day-baseten-inference-stack/

 - 2x faster inference with KV cache-aware routing https://www.baseten.co/blog/how-baseten-achieved-2x-faster-inference-with-nvidia-dynamo/

 - How Baseten multi-cloud capacity management (MCM) unifies deployments https://www.baseten.co/blog/how-baseten-multi-cloud-capacity-management-mcm-powers-cloud-self-hosted-and-hybr/#comparing-deployment-options-cloud-vs-self-hosted-vs-hybrid


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build the infrastructure and orchestration systems that deploy and run large-scale distributed LLM inference, including routing, autoscaling, scheduling, and runtime management.

 - Design, build, and operate Model APIs, with a focus on advanced inference capabilities: structured outputs (JSON mode, grammar-constrained generation), tool/function calling, and multimodal serving.

 - Implement platform fundamentals such as API versioning, validation, usage metering, quotas, and authentication.

 - Instrument deep observability (metrics, traces, logs) and build repeatable benchmarks for speed, reliability, and quality. Help set best practices for testing, release automation, and operational excellence.

 - Debug and harden complex production systems spanning Kubernetes, distributed runtimes, networking, and GPU workloads to improve reliability and scalability.

 - Partner with Inference Performance engineers and other teams to make new optimizations broadly available to customers and easy to configure.

 - Own projects end to end, from architecture through deployment, monitoring, and iteration on customer feedback. Along the way, make thoughtful tradeoffs between performance, reliability, operational simplicity, and developer experience.

 

REQUIREMENTS

 - Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - 3+ years building and operating distributed systems, backend infrastructure, or large-scale APIs where reliability, latency, and scale are first-class concerns.

 - A proven track record of owning low-latency, reliable backend services, including rate limiting, auth, quotas, metering, and migrations.

 - Infrastructure instincts with a feel for performance: profiling, tracing, capacity planning, and SLO management.

 - Comfort debugging performance and reliability issues across multiple layers of the stack, from application behavior down to runtime and infrastructure internals.

 - A strong sense of developer experience. You think about how systems are used, not just how they work.

 - Eagerness to learn new languages, frameworks, and systems, and a real interest in inference engineering. Prior ML or LLM experience isn't required, though experience with model serving or inference systems is a plus.

 - Excellent written communication and collaboration skills, including writing clear design docs and working across functions.

 

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with or contributions to LLM inference engines and frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, TGI, or Dynamo.

 - Deep Kubernetes experience, including operators and custom resources, plus familiarity with service meshes or API gateways.

 - Experience with distributed scheduling, autoscaling, or service orchestration.

 - Experience operating GPU workloads in production.

 - A background in developer-facing infrastructure or APIs, or contributions to open-source infrastructure or ML systems.

 - Familiarity with observability tooling, CI/CD systems, or release automation.



BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

 - Flexible PTO policy including company wide Winter Break (our offices are closed from Christmas Eve to New Year's Day!)

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

 - Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.

Apply now to embark on a rewarding journey in shaping the future of AI! If you are a motivated individual with a passion for machine learning and a desire to be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking team, we would love to hear from you.

You'll be responsible for building, tuning, and evolving AI agents in production environments, defining the standard for ADLC best practices along the way.

EXAMPLE PROJECTS

 - Design and build AI agents for large telecommunications and media companies that consistently outperform human agents in managing subscription churn

 - Develop and refine AI agents capable of navigating complex customer interactions, like troubleshooting a broken device and personalizing product recommendations

 - Create generalizable AI agent frameworks tailored for industry-specific use cases. See some examples in our financial services blog https://sierra.ai/blog/five-ways-to-use-ai-agents-financial-services!

 - Experiment with the latest voice models and figure out how to integrate them at scale to enterprise-grade customers


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Experience building and scaling end-to-end production systems

 - Strong technical problem-solving skills, especially in fast-changing, ambiguous environments

 - A builder and tinkerer’s mindset with high agency - you find creative ways to overcome obstacles and ship

 - Comfort working directly with customers to understand their needs and solve real-world problems

 - Excellent communication skills - clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences


EVEN BETTER...

 - Have been a founder or founding engineer - you know what it means to balance craft, ownership, and speed

 - Familiarity with tools that power today's AI agents: eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG pipelines, and prompt engineering

 - Prior experience with React, TypeScript, and/or Go

 - Previous roles where you interfaced with customers or led technical projects with external stakeholders


OUR VALUES

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all. Data quality is foundational to this process. Machines (or Large Language Models, to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans, by way of feedback. By labelling, ranking, auditing, and correcting model output, you will improve Large Language Models' performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere's technology. We are hiring Generalist professionals with broad backgrounds that span multiple consumer-facing or personal domains.

This is a judgment-driven role, not passive data entry. You will review, assess, and provide structured feedback across a broad and evolving range of tasks, evaluating, stress-testing, and improving our models on English-language data spanning multiple modalities (text, image, and structured formats such as JSON, CSV/TSV, and Markdown). This is a great opportunity for professionals with strong analytical skills to contribute to high-impact annotation projects.

Please Note: This is a part-time independent contractor position available within Canada only. We seek candidates who can commit to 16 hours per week at a CAD $30/hour contract rate. This role is BYOD 💻 (Bring Your Own Device, laptop). This position is remote.

As an Data Annotation Specialist, you will:

 - Evaluate and rank model outputs: Complete preference and comparison tasks, assessing which responses best conform to project guidelines for accuracy, helpfulness, tone, and safety, and writing clear justifications for your judgments.

 - Stress-test and break models: Probe models adversarially to surface failure modes, unsafe behavior, and capability gaps, and document reproducible cases that engineering and research teams can act on.

 - Create datasets: Author high-quality prompts, responses, and exemplars to build training and evaluation datasets, following detailed specifications and editing machine-written or human-written outputs to standard.

 - Build and apply rubrics and taxonomies: Contribute to the design of grading criteria and rubrics, then apply them consistently to produce structured, high-quality annotations across task types.

 - Annotate and correct multimodal data: Label, audit, and rectify inaccuracies across text, image, and structured data, maintaining a high standard of data integrity and accuracy.

 - Calibrate and maintain consistency: Participate in calibration exercises and inter-annotator agreement checks to align on standards, and flag ambiguous or uncovered edge cases rather than guessing, since a single misjudgment replicated at scale degrades a model.

 - Adapt to experimental work: Take on new and evolving task types as project needs shift, applying sound judgment in areas where guidelines are still being developed.

 - Report on model performance: Surface and communicate quality and performance trends in model and agent behavior, giving cross-functional partners clear, well-evidenced feedback on where models succeed, fail, and degrade.

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - 1+ years of experience in AI data annotation, LLM evaluation, content moderation, research, or a related analytical role, with exposure to quality assurance, and/or preference ranking.

 - Experience applying detailed guidelines to complex and often ambiguous content, with strong contextual and sociocultural judgment, sensitivity to nuance, tone, and register, and the ability to reason well in cases where there is no single correct answer.

 - Comfort with ambiguity: a willingness to flag unclear or uncovered edge cases rather than guess, and to work productively on novel, experimental tasks whose definitions are still evolving.

 - A sharp, curious eye for inconsistencies, subtle errors, and model failure modes, including the instinct to probe models adversarially and surface where they break. Familiarity with how large language models behave, such as hallucination, sycophancy, and instruction-following gaps, is a plus.

 - Excellent command of written English and strong reading comprehension, with the ability to clearly justify your evaluations, including why an output is correct or incorrect, high-quality or low-quality, and to write clear prompts and exemplars that explain your reasoning. Bonus points if you are fluent in another language!

 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, with the ability to maintain consistency across high-volume and monotonous tasks.

 - Comfort working with annotation platforms and structured formats such as JSON, CSV/TSV, Markdown, XML, and YAML.

 - Strong execution in a remote environment, including good time management, comfort using new tools, and the ability to work independently in a global, asynchronous team.

Candidate Journey

 - Initial Screening: Our Talent Team will review your application.

 - First Assessment: If selected to move forward, you’ll receive a multiple-choice assessment by email.

 - Second Assessment: Candidates who achieve a passing score will be contacted by a member of our team to complete a more comprehensive assessment focused on their area of expertise.

 - Video Screen: If selected to move forward, you’ll have a short video call with a member of our Operations Team.

 - Final: Selected candidates will receive an Independent Contractor Agreement.

As an independent contractor, you maintain control over how you complete your work and may work with multiple clients simultaneously, although we ask you to declare if any of these are with a direct competitor of Cohere and maintain IP confidentiality of the Cohere project. Independent contractors are not eligible for health benefits or other benefits provided to employees. Compensation for services is provided to contractors by contractors invoicing for services provided pursuant to the terms of our agreement with the contractor.

It is important to understand that as an independent contractor, continuous work is not guaranteed. The client-contractor relationship is fundamentally project-based, meaning engagements may be temporary, periodic, or intermittent based on our organizational needs and project availability. As an independent contractor, you should anticipate fluctuations in workflow and, therefore, compensation for services when Cohere does not require as many hours of services in a week.

Prospective candidates, please be advised: this role involves working with human-generated and model-generated tasks that may involve exposure to not safe for work (NSFW) text content as part of data annotation tasks, including explicit, offensive, or other inappropriate material.
